parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is one file, src/application/task-service.ts, and it handles one concern: the use cases for users, projects and tasks, all in the single class TaskService. Every method reaches stored data only through the injected TaskRepository (addUser, addProject, addTask, findTask, findProject, findUser, tasksForProject). Nothing goes around that abstraction. The common checks live in private helpers: requireProject, requireUser and requireNonEmpty, and the public methods call them consistently. There is one small duplication. The task-status check `!taskStatuses.includes(...)`, which throws DomainError("VALIDATION", "Task status is invalid"), is written out in both createTask and listTasks instead of going through a requireValidStatus helper like the other require* checks. Both copies are in the same class, are two lines each, and use the same domain constant taskStatuses, so the rule itself is still defined in one place (the domain) and only the guard is repeated. I treat this as a minor smell, not a split in the module's concern or a bypass of its abstractions, so the unit passes.
